notes: §1985:VI.6.17.4 GR3: 'Index data items and elementary FILLER data items are not affected by the execution of an INITIALIZE statement.' InitializeBinder.ExpandInitialize, the one receiver walk, returns without a store for a contained elementary item whose name is null (an explicit FILLER or an entry with no data-name) unless the statement has WITH FILLER, and for any item InitializeItemCategory gives no category, whose first arm is USAGE INDEX; both tests stand before the REPLACING qualification, so neither form of the statement stores into them, and a FILLER group is still walked for its named items. The 1985 edition reaches the rule's unconditional form because Bind's WITH FILLER flag can never be set at 85: VersionConformancePass.VisitInitializeStatement refuses the phrase below 2002 (COBOL0830, probed). Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness: an entry with no data-name, a FILLER inside a FILLER group, a FILLER in each occurrence of a table, a FILLER table, a numeric-edited FILLER, each under INITIALIZE with and without REPLACING and under INITIALIZE of one table occurrence, and index data items (elementary and under a USAGE INDEX group) beside a numeric item with and without REPLACING NUMERIC: every FILLER and index item kept its content and every named item was set. The witness exercises one FILLER between two named items and one index data item.

next.reason: 1985: "Index data items and elementary FILLER data items are not affected by the execution of an INITIALIZE statement."; 2023: "If the FILLER phrase is not specified, elementary data items with an explicit or implicit FILLER clause.". Index items stay excluded because they are not valid MOVE receivers. FILLER items are now excluded only without the new FILLER phrase; WITH FILLER initializes them, an added case.
